A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same h4rm3l research. Their complete text, equations, figures, tables and Appendices A-K support reliable comparison; the appendix pages are identical in text and rendering.

before.justification: v1 reports original attack-synthesis and six-model benchmarking results, harm-classifier validation, and defense experiments in Appendix G.

after.justification: v2 retains those original synthesis, benchmarking, classifier-validation and defense results, including the appendix experiments.

M1.justification: The compositional DSL, decorator components, three synthesis strategies, Algorithm 1 and GPT-4 harm classifier are unchanged. The appendix implementations and prompts are also identical.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same AdvBench requests and retain the same synthesis, safety-benchmarking and defense tasks. Appendix G's Alpaca and Bianchi et al. safety-instruction data are unchanged.

E2.justification: Figure 2 and Table 2 retain the same synthesis-method and low-level-expression comparisons. The attack comparators in Table 1 and defense comparisons in Appendix G are unchanged.

E3.justification: Both retain the same synthesis sampling settings, 50-request benchmark evaluations, target models and classifier-validation procedure. Appendix G's training split, fine-tuning budget and defense settings are identical.

E4.justification: The specialized-versus-generic primitive ablation, transfer analysis, composition and clustering analyses, annotation examples and defense experiments are retained unchanged. The Ethics Statement adds no empirical analysis.

E5.justification: Both report the same three-run classifier validation, standard errors in Figure 6 and stated two-standard-deviation intervals in Appendix G. No run-count, seed or uncertainty-reporting practice changes.

E6.justification: The numerical results, plots and reported findings are unchanged. Table 1 retains maximum ASRs of 94% for GPT-4o and 82% for Claude-3-haiku; Tables 2-4 also retain every result entry.

T1.justification: The composition and ASR definitions, Beta-distribution equations in Section 3, and perplexity expression in Appendix G are unchanged. No formal assumptions, derivations or proofs are added or revised.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction and conclusion retain the same contributions: a compositional attack language, bandit-based synthesis, 2,656 successful attacks, six-model benchmarking and open-source software. The scientific claims are neither strengthened nor narrowed.

C2.justification: The new Ethics Statement explicitly discusses possible undue refusals from safety filters developed using synthesized attacks and elaborates privacy risks. Existing interpretations and limitations concerning harm classification, transfer and additional Claude safety filters remain unchanged.

D1.justification: v2 adds a project-page footnote and removes v1's statement that synthesis code would be withheld except upon reasonable request. Other implementation details remain unchanged; the PDFs do not establish an actual change in code availability.

R1.justification: The cited-work set and Section 2's positioning relative to HarmBench, JailbreakBench, DSPy and other prior work are unchanged. The references merely reflow.

P1.justification: v2 adds Section 8, Ethics Statement, and removes the short Mitigating misuse paragraph from Section 6. A project footnote and minor punctuation changes accompany this localized expansion; the scientific narrative is otherwise retained.

P2.justification: The added footnote and ethics section cause text and reference reflow, and Figure 6 shifts below an existing paragraph. Figures, tables and captions retain their content and design; appendix layouts are identical.

improvement.justification: The explicit discussion of unintended refusals and privacy risks, together with a project-page pointer, modestly improves limitations and resource documentation. This gain is tempered by removing the concrete synthesis-code access policy, which makes release conditions less explicit. The scientific methods and empirical evidence remain unchanged.
